You have to realize that we usually only get a couple of windows each year where the market gives us the opportunity to make outsized returns. One already happened from April-June, and another one can open up at any time.

This is the time to dig deeper into fundamentals. Look for companies with explosive EPS growth over the next 2-3 years that are still building bases rather than chasing names after they’re already extended.

2025 and 2026 have still offered incredible opportunities if you were able to identify the leaders with exponential growth and, more importantly, stay with them.

Like I mentioned earlier this year, patience + discipline have probably been the two most important skills in 2026.

You don’t need the market to give you opportunities every week.

You just need to be prepared when the window opens.

Want to find potential market leaders BEFORE their major moves? Study CAN SLIM.

CAN SLIM is one of my favorite frameworks for finding potential market leaders, introduced by legendary William O’Neil.

C - Current earnings growth
A - Annual earnings growth
N - New products, catalysts or new highs
S - Supply + demand
L - Leaders, not laggards
I - Institutional sponsorship
M - Market direction 

I spent some time screening AI + Tech names using this framework, while also looking for strong relative strength + stocks still building bases rather than chasing extended breakouts.

A few names on my radar:
$NVDA $ANET $PLTR $CRWD $MU
$RBRK $NET $FTNT $PANW $LITE 
$SMTC $AMD $CLS $NOW $SNOW 
$DDOG $CRDO $FORM $HPE $COHU
$VICR $FPS $IMOS $ASML $TSM 

Not every name will check every CAN SLIM box at the same time - and even the best company can be a bad entry if you’re chasing it after a major move.

The real edge is finding companies where earnings are accelerating + relative strength is improving + institutions are accumulating while the stock is still building a healthy base. That’s when I want the name on my radar

Fundamentals tell me WHAT to own. Technicals tell me WHEN to build the position.

Mastering Volatility: 
Why Trimming Into Strength Protects Your Capital

Choppy, mean-reverting markets have a habit of chewing up breakouts and triggering stops. When the tape gets tough, protecting your open capital requires moving past ego and actively managing your risk.

Here is a core rule for navigating high-volatility environments:

Trim Into Strength: 
When you have a cushion on winning positions, take partial profits into strength.

Pay for Risk: 
Using realized gains to "pay for risk" reduces your overall exposure and lowers your break-even points.

De-Risk to Stay Calm: 
Trimming removes emotional friction, giving you the psychological and financial cushion needed to withstand normal market noise without panic-selling.

When pivots fail and the market rejects new entries, stepping on the sidelines isn't quitting, it's capital preservation. Let your strong trends work, cut your losers quickly, and keep your dry powder ready for when real trend continuity returns.

US10Y at 5.25%, Again — A Swing Trader’s Perspective

Many are paying attention to the US 10Y breaching 5.25% — a level last seen in May 2007, roughly 5 months before the market peaked ahead of the Global Financial Crisis sell off.

The historical comparison is interesting, but 5.25% itself does not necessarily signal another 2007. What matters is the potential economic impact of sustained higher rates. As the cost of money rises, refinancing becomes more expensive, interest expenses increase, leverage becomes harder to carry and asset valuations can face pressure. eg. Data center operators face higher costs to finance and service billions of dollars in infrastructure debt, while also will be competing with government bond issuers for the same pool of capital at a higher cost of funding for their next tranche of debt, and homeowners rolling over mortgages face higher debt-service costs and substantial spike in their monthly repayment.

For short term swing traders, the historical parallel itself matters less. What matters is the potential for a higher volatility environment. If that volatility materializes, the opportunity is to remain flexible and capitalize on high reward-to-risk setups, particularly on the inverse side of the market when the technical setup and execution window align.

One way to prepare is to build a separate arsenal of highly liquid inverse instruments of watchlist eg. $SQQQ $SOXS $LABD $TZA $UVIX. At least when the market presents the right setup, you're prepared to act rather than scrambling to find the vehicle after the move has already started.
